extracted.intended_audience: general readers, media researchers, and people interested in the history and controversies of the newspaper Le Monde
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting standards and evaluative criteria for journalistic practice and news reporting as illustrated by the controversies, legal cases, and initiatives around the French newspaper Le Monde. Useful for assessing probity, sourcing, transparency, conflicts of interest, and legal risks in newspaper journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poll reporting transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing poll results, disclose polling dates, partner institute, sampling details and subsample sizes — e.g. the page notes Le Monde headlined 'Marine Le Pen arrive en tête parmi les jeunes de 18-24 ans' based on a CSA study whose 'sous-échantillon des jeunes 18-24 ans comportait moins de 200 personnes', a fact the paper did not signal to readers and which alarmed the Commission des sondages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report poll field dates, full sampling methodology and any small subsample sizes (explicitly flagging when subsamples are small) so readers can judge statistical reliability. Cite partner polling institutes and note differences across polls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and transparency in editorial evaluations/fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact‑checking/ranking projects must strive for impartiality and transparency; critics (e.g., Vincent Glad, Daniel Schneidermann) argued that expressing an 'impartial and transparent' judgement is difficult and that being both 'judge and party' undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and publish transparent criteria and methods for any media ranking or fact‑checking tool; disclose potential biases and avoid presenting subjective rankings as neutral facts. Anticipate and document limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid judge-and-party conflicts when ranking media
rubrics_metrics.description: Rankings (like Decodex/Decoders) were criticized for privileging professional media and potentially favoring certain outlets — the page reports concerns that the ranking 'privilégie les médias professionnels'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure third‑party review or open methodology to reduce appearance of favoritism; provide clear rationale for categorizations and allow appeals or corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source verification and contrasting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts criticized Le Monde for using information from TRACFIN that 'confère une apparente crédibilité' without alerting readers to its non‑contradictory nature and for failing 'à la prudence' in not sufficiently verifying sources; similar criticisms underpinned several defamation rulings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify source claims independently, contrast data with other evidence, and explicitly inform readers when information is partial, unilateral, or unverified. Avoid presenting single, uncorroborated official notes as definitive proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of reply and giving voice to subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgments faulted the paper for 'ne donnant pas la parole' to the person concerned and for publishing unilaterally‑sourced allegations, contributing to defamation findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek and include response from people or organizations the report criticizes; when unable to obtain comment, state that explicitly and explain attempts made to reach them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect presumption of innocence
rubrics_metrics.description: Le Monde was condemned for infringing the 'présomption d'innocence' in reporting on Pierre Falcone; reporting on alleged criminality must preserve presumption of innocence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting allegations, clearly label them as such, avoid definitive language implying guilt before legal determination, and include context about legal status of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid defamatory or unverified accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple court condemnations for diffamation are recorded (e.g., against Julien Dray, John Malkovich, others); the Tribunal suprême found that 'l'information publiée n'était pas véridique' and that journalists 'n'ayant pas suffisamment vérifié ses sources' led to harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm factual accuracy before publication, document checks, and be prepared to correct and indemnify if errors cause reputational harm. Apply heightened verification to claims that could damage honor or reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution with anonymous sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The page highlights criticism of the Figaro's use of anonymous sources to discredit a competitor; anonymous sourcing used to attack rivals drew particular censure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit use of anonymous sources, especially when accusations target individuals or organizations; when used, explain reasons for anonymity and the degree of corroboration supporting the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage conflicts of interest and recusal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal controversy arose over an appointment (Rayan Nezzar) creating perceived 'risks de conflit d'intérêts' and the Société des rédacteurs seized the ethics committee to 'évaluer les précautions prises'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement clear conflict‑of‑interest policies, disclose personal or familial links that could affect coverage, evaluate and document precautions (e.g., recusal, editorial oversight) and refer issues to an ethics committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence and disclosure of funding/partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: The page notes partnerships and funding (e.g., Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation support for Le Monde Afrique) and states partners must 'respectent les valeurs du Monde et l’indépendance éditoriale de sa rédaction'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose external funding and partnerships and ensure contractual safeguards protecting editorial independence; inform readers when partners support specific coverage areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unfair commercial denigration of competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Le Monde was condemned for 'concurrence déloyale par dénigrement' against FranceSoir — the judge found the criticism could 'porter une atteinte grave à son modèle économique'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing criticisms that amount to commercial denigration without factual basis; ensure critiques of competitors are factual, proportionate and clearly distinguished from opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be responsive to reader concerns about sensitive imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Following an investigation, Le Monde 'retire ces images, «qui ont pu choquer»' after publishing graphic imagery (a 'mur de Gaza' collage) that some readers found shocking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential for imagery to shock or traumatize readers, weigh news value vs. harm, and be willing to remove or contextualize images that cause justified reader distress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize editorial stances to avoid perceived cultural or geopolitical bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorials were criticized for appearing 'européocentrée' or for taking stances that outside observers viewed as advising or legitimizing actions (e.g., about Qatar during the 2022 World Cup); critics argued such stances risked lacking credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide broad context, acknowledge perspective and limitations, and include voices from affected regions to reduce perception of cultural centrism or external moralizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact‑checking tools: label and explain source reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Le Monde launched tools (Décodeurs, Décodex) to fight fake news — the initiatives aim to help readers 'démasquer les fake news' but were also critiqued for method/transparency issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publishing reliability labels or fact‑checks, make methodology public, allow corrections, and avoid presenting binary labels without nuance; provide links to evidence and explain criteria for categorizations.
